senses.gloss:
Duś-carman, ‘afflicted with a skin disease,’ occurs in the taittirīya Saṃhitā and brāhmaṇa. The disease meant is probably leprosy, the usual name of which is kilāsa.
Foot notes ii. 1, 4, 3; 5, 1, 7.
i. 7, 8, 3.
pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa, xiv. 3, 17; xxiii. 16, 11; taittirīya Āraṇyaka v. 4, 12.

Duṣ-ṭarītu, ‘hard to defeat,’ is the name of a king of the Sṛñjayas, who was deposed from a principality that had existed for ten generations, but was re-instated by cākra sthapati in spite of the resistance of balhika prātipīya, according to the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa.
Foot notes xii. 9, 3, 1 et seq. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 1, 205-207.

Dūṣīkā, ‘rheum of the eyes,’ is mentioned as a disease in the Atharvaveda and later.
Foot notes xvi. 6, 8.
kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xxxiv. 12; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxv. 9; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, iii. 1, 3, 10.
